fr.elements: Main Building; Secondary Building; Vehicle Parking Area; Internal Drive Aisle; Access Road; Landscaped Area; Landscaped Area; Walkway; Dumpster Enclosure; Street Frontage
fr.considerations: Multiple Structures; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Single Access Point
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the access road entrance with a clearly visible address sign readable from both directions of approach.

• Mark the secondary building with its own unit or building identifier so responders can distinguish it from the main building on arrival.

• Keep the internal drive aisle clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach both structures.

• Identify and mark any secondary path to the rear of the property, even if informal, to give responders an alternative route when the single access point is blocked.

• Keep the dumpster enclosure positioned so it does not narrow or obstruct the drive aisle used by emergency vehicles.

• Trim vegetation along the access road and drive aisle to maintain overhead and side clearance for fire apparatus.

• Trim vegetation near both building exteriors to maintain a clear path for responders moving on foot around the structures.

• Designate and mark a staging area near the access road entrance where additional emergency vehicles can hold without blocking the drive aisle.

• Post a site map at the property entrance showing the location of both buildings, the drive aisle, and any utility shut-offs.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Large Trees; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Building; Vegetation Near Building; Large Paved Area; Open Paved Area; Scattered Shrubs; Limited Rear Access
wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove or trim shrubs and vegetation growing directly against building exteriors where contact with the structure is visible.
• Thin or remove shrubs concentrated near building walls to create separation between plants and the structure.
• Trim lower branches on large trees near buildings to reduce the connection between ground-level vegetation and the tree canopy.
• Thin trees within clusters near structures to reduce the density of vegetation immediately around buildings.
• Keep the large paved area and open paved areas clear of any vegetation growing through cracks or along edges.
• Clear vegetation and debris from the rear of the building to improve access for emergency responders where rear access is limited.
• Keep a clear path around the perimeter of all structures to allow responders to move freely between the front and rear of buildings.
